bugs.description: The page-jump input is a native <input type="number" max={totalPages}>. Typing a value above totalPages (e.g. 999) and clicking 'Ir' does NOT clamp to the last page as required by the spec ('limitam valores fora da faixa e exibem a página escolhida') -- instead the browser's native HTML5 constraint validation blocks the form submit entirely (tooltip 'Value must be less than or equal to 3'), so the Go button is inert for out-of-range values and the page never changes. Low-end clamping to page 1 also never executes because the same submit is blocked before React's onSubmit/go() logic runs.
bugs.evidence: Browser check catalog-pagination-jump-to-page: after filling '999' and clicking data-testid=catalog-page-go-button-top, page stayed at 'Página 2 de 3 · 100 títulos' instead of clamping to 'Página 3 de 3'. Debug screenshot confirms native validation tooltip 'Value must be less than or equal to 3' over the input, and inputValue()='999' with checkValidity()=false. Backend/data layer is healthy (100 items imported and paginated correctly across valid pages, confirmed by catalog-pagination-48-per-page and catalog-pagination-nav-controls passing) -- this is a frontend-only control defect in components/CatalogGrid.tsx's Pagination form.

action_items.item: Fix CatalogGrid.tsx Pagination jump form: either remove the native max attribute (or set it very high) and clamp purely in the go() handler, or intercept keydown/clamp before relying on form submit, so out-of-range values (too high or too low/zero) are clamped and submitted instead of being silently blocked by native HTML5 validation.
